_meta.what: Every 2026 team's car derived from its two Silverstone qualifying laps (OpenF1) by the inverse vehicle dynamics of concept/tools/derive-car.js: PhysicalCar-shaped estimates with bootstrap mean ± sd, fit residuals and a teammate held-out check. Red Bull's full write-up: concept/data/redbull-2026-derived.json and docs/concept/REDBULL-DERIVED.md.
caveats: ICE power is the same assumption for every PU (η_th 0.475 × the regulated 833 kW fuel flow). CdA_c is therefore conditional: an ICE weaker than assumed shows up as a HIGHER CdA_c (the 350 kW deployment anchor needs more drag to explain the same acceleration), a stronger one as lower. Compare CdA_c directly only between teams sharing a PU.

If a car never reaches 350 kW of deployment on its best exits, the anchor cannot be met: CdA_c is then the median of the other teams (cda_anchor.ok = false) and top3_peak_dc_kw shows the deployment that implies.
ΔCdA (Straight Mode) is one value for all cars, measured on all laps.
μ_y and ClA are strongly anti-correlated; μ_y·ClA (muClA) is the better-determined quantity.

Bootstrap sd covers lap-to-lap and corner/straight/zone sampling only; systematic bands come on top (η_th ±0.025 -> CdA ±0.09; x/y smoothing -> ClA +0.6/-0.4, see redbull-2026-derived.json sensitivity).
Aero balance, CoG height, tracks, wheelbase, tyre radius and fuel are assumptions, as for Red Bull. Masses use the reported April over-minimum figures.
_meta.multi_circuit: Circuit specifics (lap files, corner markers, weather, Straight Mode zones, recharge limit) are in the CIRCUITS registry of the tool. A joint fit across circuits would share μ, the PU and the ClA/CdA efficiency of each car, with a per-circuit wing level (ClA and CdA scale).
